result:
This confirms the complete set: only `activity-service.ts`, `usage-service.ts`, `search-service.ts`, and `webhook-service.ts` call `subscribe("issue.created", ...)`. `event-registry.ts` wires them but doesn't itself handle the event; `notification-service.ts` subscribes to other events only; `event-bus.ts` defines the bus itself.

When a new issue is created, `IssueService.createIssue` (src/server/services/issue-service.ts:71) calls `emit("issue.created", ...)`. Four modules register handlers that react to that event via `subscribe("issue.created", ...)`, all wired up through `registerEventHandlers()` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`:

- `src/server/services/activity-service.ts` — records an activity-feed entry for the new issue.
- `src/server/services/usage-service.ts` — updates usage/metering counters.
- `src/server/services/search-service.ts` — indexes the new issue for search.
- `src/server/services/webhook-service.ts` — enqueues an outbound webhook delivery.

`src/server/services/issue-service.ts` only publishes the event; `src/types/event.ts`, `src/types/activity.ts`, `src/schemas/activity.ts`, `src/schemas/webhook.ts`, and `src/components/domain/activity/activity-labels.ts` merely declare/label the `"issue.created"` string and don't register handlers; `notification-service.ts` subscribes to different events (`issue.assigned`, `issue.overdue`, `comment.created`, `member.joined`), not this one.

ANSWER: src/server/services/activity-service.ts, src/server/services/usage-service.ts, src/server/services/search-service.ts, src/server/services/webhook-service.ts
